source: NAVMED Leadership Course Catalog Medical Corps Edition

courses.name: Division Officer Leadership Course (DIVOLC)
courses.description: First course in Medical Department Officer's Learning Continuum. Provides Junior Officers tools to function as effective leaders at Division Officer level.
courses.requirement: Service school requirement for all officers per MILPERSMAN 1301-906
courses.notes: Required for officers who attended ODS after Jan 1, 2018

courses.name: Intermediate Leadership Course (ILC)
courses.description: Provides intermediate-level Officers with Navy leadership skills required for next milestones and positions of increased responsibility. Replaces Department Head Leadership Course (DHLC).
courses.registration: CeTARS/eNTRS via SEAT officer. Register at least 5 weeks prior.

courses.name: Senior Leadership Course (SLC)
courses.description: 5-day seminar for Senior Officers at O5 and above. Designed to facilitate formal leadership and ethics education to support Fleet Centered Leader Development.
courses.requirement: Recommended for senior officers heading to fleet-wide positions

courses.name: Basic Readiness Officer Course (BROC)
courses.description: Second course in Medical Department Officer's Learning Continuum. Four-unit online course introducing organization, structure, business practices, and operational policies of Naval Medical Department.

courseIds.topic: Navy Medicine DIVO/DH Functions and Sailorization

courses.name: Advanced Readiness Officer Course (AROC)
courses.description: Advanced readiness training for Medical Department Officers. Currently on pause pending Job, Duty, Task Analysis (JDTA) and Training Requirements Review (TRR).
courses.status: ON PAUSE - Check NMLPDC website for updates
courses.registration: Check NMLPDC Academic Course Registration when available
courses.notes: Updates coming - check website for most current information

courses.name: JPME I - Fleet Seminar Program
courses.description: Naval War College Joint Professional Military Education Phase I delivered to students who cannot attend in-residence. Expands critical and creative thinking for decision-making in maritime domain.
courses.requirement: Required for 67B Expeditionary Medicine AQD. Important for senior leadership positions.
courses.format: In-person seminars (one evening per week, 3 hours)
courses.eligibility: O3+ for Navy/USMC/USCG, O4+ for other services, GS11+ for civilians
courses.funding: Naval War College provides materials on loan basis

courses.name: JPME I - Naval Command and Staff Online
courses.description: Online program educating students on fundamentals of U.S. national security policy, military strategy, and their relationship. Five educational modules.
courses.eligibility: O3+ for Navy/USMC/USCG, O4+ for other services, GS11+ for civilians

courses.name: Healthcare Management Course (HCM)
courses.description: Tri-service course for first-time clinical supervisors providing administrative tools to manage clinical areas. Topics include civilian personnel, contracting, budgeting, quality management.
courses.registration: Self-nomination via JKO after completing Phase 1 prerequisites
courses.jkoEnrollment: Search for course US300 after completing Phase 1

courses.name: Intermediate Executive Skills Course (IESC)
courses.description: Education and training on leadership and management skills necessary to serve in intermediate-level leadership position within DHA MTF.
courses.targetGrade: O4-5, E7-8, GS11-13 (minimum O3, E6, GS9)
courses.requirement: Recommended for intermediate-level leaders in DHA facilities
courses.registration: Self-nomination via JKO after completing Phase 1 prerequisites
courses.jkoEnrollment: Search for course US400 after completing Phase 1

courses.name: Capstone for MHS Leaders Course
courses.description: Pinnacle educational event for senior MHS leaders. Speakers include Service Surgeons General, ASD(HA), DHA Director. Provides firsthand knowledge for MTF commanders.
courses.requirement: For new lead agents, commanders of larger facilities, command surgeons
courses.registration: Corps Chief's Office nomination - not self-nomination

courses.name: Senior Leader Legal Course (SLLC)
courses.description: 3-day course to prepare O5-O6 commanding officers, executive officers, and senior enlisted for legal issues as command triad. Covers UCMJ, admin separations, court-martial, ethics.
courses.requirement: For COs, XOs, and SELs heading to command positions
courses.registration: eNTRS for Navy students. Detailers register incoming COs/XOs.

poc.name: LT Zach Osterloh
poc.title: Fleet Leader Legal Training Program Manager

courses.name: Surface Warfare Medical Department Officer Indoctrination Course (SWMDOIC)
courses.description: Orientation to Fleet operations for Medical Department Officers with ship assignments. Covers medical assets of surface vessels, admin requirements, preventive/occupational health.
courses.requirement: Training prerequisite for Surface Warfare Medical Department Officer Qualification

poc.address: 34101 Farenholt Avenue, Bldg 14, San Diego, CA 92134

courses.name: Commander Amphibious Task Force Surgeon Course (CATF-S)
courses.description: Prepares Medical Corps Officers for unique challenges of being CATF Surgeon. Upon graduation, eligible for assignment as CATF/ESG Surgeon and OIC of Fleet Surgical Team.
courses.requirement: Satisfies MAP requirements for Echelon III Command and Control
courses.registration: CeTARS/eNTRS. Priority given to those filling or with orders to CATF-S billet.
courses.funding: Parent Command (most candidates need local funding or no-cost status)

poc.address: 34101 Farenholt Avenue, Bldg 14, San Diego, CA 92134

courses.name: MedXellence
courses.description: 40 hours of continuing education for current and aspiring MHS leaders. Combination of lectures, discussions, and small-group case study exercises based on real-world MHS scenarios.
courses.requirement: For rising MHS executives who wish to be educated on MHS relevant issues

sessions.registration: Self-nominate or supervisor nomination via USU website

courses.registration: Online nomination. Selection based on Service, rank, corps, job title balance.
courses.eligibility: Must have at least 2 years of service remaining

courses.name: Navy Medicine Quality, Safety, and Leadership Academy (NMQSLA)
courses.description: HRO training for Navy Medicine leaders. Didactic and interactive sessions on HRO, quality, and safety concepts. Includes Capstone Project developing HRO initiative.
courses.requirement: Mandated for milestone and command billets per BUMEDINSTs 1410.1 and 1412.D. Mandated for SEM billets per BUMEDINST 1412.2 (FY26+).
courses.duration: 3-day Kick-Off + 5 Virtual Classroom sessions + Capstone presentation

sessions.registration: NMQSLA Support Team reaches out to identified billets. Others can request via email.

courses.registration: Contact NMQSLA Support Team to be added to waitlist
courses.funding: Free for service members (travel if applicable varies by Cohort)

courses.name: Interagency Institute for Federal Health Leaders
courses.description: Two-week course for seasoned federal health care executives examining current health care policy and management issues. Faculty includes research leaders and national policy decision-makers.
courses.requirement: For senior officers tracking toward Executive Medicine
courses.registration: Corps Chief's Office nomination - not self-nomination
courses.quotaNote: 11 quotas for Navy Medicine shared among four Corps

courses.name: Navy Senior Leadership Seminar (NSLS)
courses.description: 5-day executive education program on strategic thinking, goal setting, risk management, financial management, innovative thinking, strategic communication, and organizational change.
courses.requirement: For senior Navy Officers, Civilians, and Command Master Chiefs

sessions.location: Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, CA (or Virtual)

courses.registration: Quotas managed by Navy Medicine Medical Department Corps Career Planners. Nomination via Chain of Command.
courses.quotaNote: 2 seats for Navy Medicine shared among all Corps
courses.funding: NPS covers tuition. Parent command provides travel/lodging/per-diem for in-person.

poc.organization: Center for Executive Education - Naval Postgraduate School

67A.name: Executive Medicine
67A.description: Required per NDAA and BUMEDINST 1412.1B for Command Qualification Program (2D1 AQD)

requirements.experience: Department/Division Head (Clinical, Administrative, or Science) 2-year minimum tour
courses: JMESI Intermediate Executive Skills Course or equivalent
requirements.operational: One of: 2-year operational tour, combined deployment experience, or operational educational training

67B.name: Expeditionary Medicine
67B.description: For officers with warfare designator and JPME completion

requirements.courses: 7 Core and 7 Additional courses (contact JMESP PM for list)

67G.name: Managed Care
67G.description: For officers with 67A and managed care experience

requirements.experience: 1 year Healthcare Business Operations at HQ (DHA, BUMED, Region, Market) or MTF directorate/department

aweOpportunities.name: Assistant Professor — USUHS or Affiliated Program
aweOpportunities.description: Serve on faculty at the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences (USUHS) or an affiliated military medical school. Teaches medical students, supports graduate programs, and builds the academic record needed for associate/full professor progression.
benefits: Demonstrates academic commitment and subject matter expertise
Builds toward 67A (Executive Medicine) AQD prerequisites
Strengthens record for senior MTF and academic command billets
Opportunity to publish and build research portfolio
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Request via detailer. USUHS faculty billets listed in OPNAV billet database. Academic rank conferred by USUHS based on credentials and experience.

contact.organization: USUHS Department of Military and Emergency Medicine
contact.note: Contact your detailer and corps chief office for billet availability

aweOpportunities.name: Associate / Full Professor — USUHS
aweOpportunities.description: Senior faculty position at USUHS. Leads curriculum development, mentors junior faculty, and contributes to DoD medical education policy. Typically filled by CDR/CAPT with established research or clinical education track record.
benefits: Senior academic credential — positions officer for SES or academic executive roles post-service
Directly supports USUHS mission and Medical Corps strategic intent
Qualifies officer for 67A AQD if not already held
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Nomination by USUHS Department Chair in coordination with corps chief. Academic rank promotion through USUHS process.

contact.note: Coordinate with Medical Corps Career Planner (CAPT O'Sullivan)

aweOpportunities.name: Researcher / Principal Investigator — DoD Research Command
aweOpportunities.description: Serve as PI or co-investigator at a DoD research command: Naval Medical Research Command (NMRC), Walter Reed Army Institute of Research (WRAIR), Naval Aerospace Medical Research Laboratory (NAMRL), or CDMRP-funded program. Drives peer-reviewed publications and grants.
benefits: Peer-reviewed publications strengthen promotion record at all levels
May count toward 6OC (Clinical Investigator Program) AQD if enrolled in CIP
Opens academic and industry pathways post-service
Demonstrates intellectual breadth beyond clinical care
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Apply to Clinical Investigator Program (CIP) for structured research track, or request research billet directly via detailer. CDMRP intramural funding available separately.

contact.note: CIP applications open annually — contact corps chief for CIP nomination cycle

aweOpportunities.name: Clinical Investigator Program (CIP) Fellowship
aweOpportunities.description: Formal 2–3 year DoD research fellowship leading to a graduate degree (PhD, MPH, or Master's in research discipline). Graduates earn 6OC AQD and establish the academic foundation for a research-focused career track.
benefits: 6OC AQD upon completion
Advanced degree (PhD or Master's) funded by Navy
Positions officer for research command leadership and academic appointments
Highly competitive — demonstrates selectivity on promotion record
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Annual call for nominations through corps chief office. Highly competitive — requires research proposal and faculty sponsor.

contact.note: Contact Medical Corps Career Planner for annual nomination timeline

aweOpportunities.name: BUMED / OPNAV Staff Medical Officer
aweOpportunities.description: Staff billet at Bureau of Medicine and Surgery (BUMED) or OPNAV N093 (Surgeon General staff). Engages in policy development, resource allocation, and strategic planning at the enterprise level. Essential for O6 and flag-track officers.
benefits: Builds strategic and policy competencies required for 67A AQD
Visibility with senior Navy Medicine leadership
Critical for flag officer track — most flag nominees have HQ staff experience
Develops joint and interagency skills
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Request via detailer. BUMED billets are competitive — communicate interest to corps chief office 18–24 months before EAOS.

contact.note: Discuss with your detailer during your 18-month window

aweOpportunities.name: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Staff Officer
aweOpportunities.description: Joint staff billet within DHA supporting the military health system. Covers healthcare operations, policy, and resource management across all services. Satisfies joint duty assignment (JDA) credit toward O7 eligibility.
benefits: Counts toward Joint Duty Assignment (JDA) requirement for O7 consideration
Interagency and joint service exposure
Contributes to 67A and 67G AQD pathways
Visibility across all military services and DoD health leadership
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Request through detailer. Joint billets require JPME I for full credit. Apply at least 18 months prior.

contact.note: Joint duty credit requires JPME I — complete JPME before or during DHA tour

aweOpportunities.name: Health Policy Fellowship (White House / Congress)
aweOpportunities.description: Competitive fellowship placing officers on Capitol Hill, White House staff, federal agencies (HHS, VA, OMB), or think tanks. Robert Wood Johnson Health Policy Fellowship is the most common route. Builds senior policy and legislative experience.
benefits: Exceptional visibility — highly selective
Builds legislative and executive branch relationships
Positions officer for senior advisory and policy roles post-service
Strengthens executive leadership narrative for promotion boards
aweOpportunities.howToApply: RWJ fellowship opens annually (applications in fall). Congressional fellowship through AUSA/AMA pathways. Requires CDR/LCDR and demonstrated policy interest.

contact.organization: Robert Wood Johnson Health Policy Fellowship Program
contact.note: Requires strong endorsement — discuss with mentor and corps chief

aweOpportunities.name: GME Residency Program Director
aweOpportunities.description: Lead a Graduate Medical Education (GME) residency program at an NMRTC. Responsible for ACGME accreditation compliance, curriculum, faculty development, and resident training. Demonstrates senior academic and administrative leadership.
benefits: Senior educational leadership credential
ACGME accreditation experience directly applicable to senior MTF positions
Builds toward 67A (Executive Medicine) AQD
Mentorship of the next generation of Navy physicians
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Nominated by MTF command. Requires specialty board certification and prior faculty experience preferred. Coordinate with NMRTC command and specialty corps chief.

contact.note: Discuss with your MTF Chief of Staff or GME committee chair

aweOpportunities.name: NMLPDC Faculty — Leadership Development
aweOpportunities.description: Serve on faculty at the Navy Medicine Leader and Professional Development Command (NMLPDC). Instructs DIVOLC, ILC, SLC, or other leadership programs. Develops curriculum and shapes officer professional development Navy-wide.
benefits: Deep engagement with leadership development programs
Builds facilitator and curriculum design skills
Strengthens 67A AQD qualifications
High visibility with Navy Medicine leadership
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Request via detailer. NMLPDC located at Bethesda, MD (Walter Reed National Military Medical Center campus).

contact.organization: Navy Medicine Leader and Professional Development Command (NMLPDC)

aweOpportunities.name: OCONUS / Operational Deployed Tour
aweOpportunities.description: Overseas tour at an OCONUS MTF (Germany, Japan, Spain, Bahrain), deployed with a Marine unit (battalion/regimental surgeon), Fleet Surgical Team (FST), or theater medical command. Builds operational credibility critical for senior promotions.
benefits: Operational credibility — strongly weighted by promotion boards
Contributes to warfare qualification AQDs (FMF, SW)
Required for some senior operational billets (CATF Surgeon, GHE staff)
Joint and multinational medical engagement experience
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Coordinate with detailer. Volunteer for deployment through parent command. OCONUS billets require PCS orders.

contact.note: Communicate OCONUS / operational preference to your detailer at the 24-month window

aweOpportunities.name: Joint Duty Assignment (JDA)
aweOpportunities.description: Assignment to a joint command: Joint Staff (Pentagon), CENTCOM/INDOPACOM/EUCOM surgeon staff, SOCOM, or qualifying DHA billet. Earns Joint Duty Assignment credit — required for officers competitive for O7 selection.
benefits: Joint Duty credit required for O7 (flag) consideration per Goldwater-Nichols
Interservice and strategic-level experience
Exposure to combatant command medical operations
Strengthens flag officer packet significantly
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Must have JPME I for full joint credit. Request JDA-coded billets through detailer. JPME II (Naval War College resident course) enhances competitive standing.

contact.note: JPME I completion is prerequisite — complete before or simultaneously with JDA tour

aweOpportunities.name: Special Operations Command Medical Officer (SOF)
aweOpportunities.description: Embed with Navy Special Warfare (NSW/SEAL teams), Marine Raiders (MARSOC), or Joint Special Operations Command (JSOC) as a Special Operations medical officer. Highly competitive, requires additional training (SOCM, SEAL/SOF screening).
benefits: Exceptional operational credibility
Contributes to FMF/EXW AQD pathways
Highly distinctive on promotion record
Builds trauma, austere medicine, and small-unit leadership skills
aweOpportunities.howToApply: Volunteer through command. Requires SOCM qualification and physical screening. Coordinate with Naval Special Warfare Command Medical Officer.

contact.note: SOCM course required — 18+ weeks. Apply 18–24 months before desired start
